title: Multi-stage assessment sprint and exemplar evidence wallet
content:
Purpose:
This working doc defines a compact, multi-stage candidate assessment sprint aimed at accelerating hiring decisions for mid-senior engineering roles while preserving signal fidelity. It also defines an "exemplar evidence wallet" (structured artifacts to gather during the process) so hiring managers and interviewers have a shared view of what ‘good’ looks like.

Scope and constraints:
- Role focus: Mid-Senior Software Engineer (inference/runtime focus), adaptable to SRE and infra-engineer hires with small tweaks.
- Timebox: 2 weeks from first screen to offer decision (with optional 1-week extension for targeted deep-dives).
- Candidate experience priorities: predictable timeline, clear prep guidance, single point-of-contact.
- Hiring team priorities: high signal per interview minute, consistent rubric, minimal redundant exercises.

Sprint overview (timeline):
Day 0: Recruiter outreach + candidate packet (role brief, sample prompts, scheduling windows).
Day 1: 30-min recruiter screen (logistics, motivators, basics).
Day 2-3: 45-min technical screen (PR-style code problem OR systems reasoning), interviewer fills rubric.
Day 4: Short async take-home (2–4 hours) for candidates passing the screen. Deliverable: small patch, short infra runbook, or focused debug write-up.
Day 7: Live pairing session (90 minutes): two interviewers, one on systems/design + one on code/ownership.
Day 8–9: Culture/behavioral + team-fit sync (45 minutes).
Day 10: Hiring committee review + evidence consolidation. Decision within 48 hrs.

Assessment flow and artifacts to collect (exemplar evidence wallet):
- Recruiter notes: candidate motivators, salary band alignment, permit/relocation constraints.
- Technical screen rubric: quick-signal checklist (algorithmic reasoning, debugging instincts, problem decomposition).
- Take-home deliverable: repo link + README with rationale and trade-offs. Checklist: completeness, test coverage, clarity of assumptions, infra/safety considerations.
- Pairing session recording notes (interviewer highlights): design diagram, latency/cost trade-offs discussed, approximation strategies used, follow-up questions.
- Behavioral anchor examples: 3 STAR-style answers tied to collaboration, drive for impact, and operational responsibility.
- References summary (if collected early): verification of scope of work, collaboration style, ramp speed.

Interview rubrics (single-page standardized):
1) Technical (weight 45%):
  - Problem framing and constraints (0–4): did candidate clarify inputs, outputs, and failure modes?
  - Correctness & algorithmic choices (0–6): solution quality, edge cases, trade-offs.
  - Execution (0–4): ability to write readable code or psuedocode, tests, and iterate.
  - Operational thinking (0–3): monitoring, rollback, SLO considerations for changes.
  - Communication (0–3): clear narration and seeking feedback.
2) System design (weight 30%):
  - Requirements scoping (0–4), capacity & latency reasoning (0–5), partitioning and dataflow (0–4), failure modes & mitigation (0–4), cost/ops trade-offs (0–3).
3) Culture & Collaboration (weight 25%):
  - Ownership examples (0–5), cross-team communication (0–4), learning orientation & feedback receptivity (0–3), hiring & mentorship inclination (0–3).

Scoring and decision guidance:
- Normalize scores to a 100-point scale using weights above.
- Red flags (automatic fail or require committee): dishonest take-home, inability to accept feedback in live session, critical gaps in operational safety awareness for infra-facing roles.
- Borderline band (70–79): recommend an extended take-home or second pairing focused on the gap area.
- Strong (>=80): proceed to reference checks + comp conversation.

Onboarding micro-plan (first 14 days) — shortened for rapid impact:
Day 0 (prestart): IT access, repo list, onboarding checklist, buddy assigned.
Day 1: Orientation (company values, team goals), 1:1 with manager, review first-week goals.
Day 2–3: Shadow pairing on a low-risk bug or tooling fix; small PR target.
Day 4–7: Ownership-lite task (incubator ticket) with explicit success criteria and rollout plan.
Day 8–10: Deep-dive sessions (architecture, infra runbooks, on-call handbook).
Day 11: Feedback checkpoint with manager + buddy.
Day 14: First-sprint demo + retrospective and 30/60/90 plan draft.

Decision committee checklist (for the 48-hour review):
- Evidence wallet complete? (screen rubric, take-home, pairing notes, behavioral answers).
- Score normalization documented in the candidate card.
- Manager sign-off on ramp plan and suggested impact in first 90 days.
- Compensation range cleared by recruiter and people ops.

Interviewer playbook (quick bullets for consistent behavior):
- Use the rubric template for every interview — no freeform scores.
- Capture verbatim candidate statements for behavioral anchors.
- If you ask a follow-up, note the question and why you asked it.
- Avoid excessive domain-specific puzzles unless role requires it — prefer system scenarios tied to our product (inference latency, batch size trade-offs, model quantization).

Unresolved questions / experiments to run in next 3 months:
- Does a 2-hour take-home produce materially different signal vs 4-hour? (run A/B with two cohorts).
- Evaluate whether adding a short operational incident simulation improves SRE hire selection.
- Explore an anonymized initial screen to reduce unconscious bias for first triage.

Appendix: candidate packet template (to send at scheduling) — short checklist for candidates:
- Role brief and expected first-90-day impact.
- Sample pairing prompt (so they know the style).
- Take-home expectations, honor code, and submission instructions.
- What to expect on the day: interviewers' roles, duration, and feedback timing.

Owner notes:
- Intend to pilot with 12 hires (3 hiring squads) over next quarter.
- Track conversion metrics: response-to-offer time, accept rate, hiring manager satisfaction score, new-hire 30-day impact.
- Please annotate this doc with local changes per team; keep a single canonical Confluence page referenced in linked_artifacts.
